'''Poni Altar''' (Japanese: '''ポニのさいだん''' ''Poni Altar'') is a location in the [[Pokémon Adventures]] {{pkmn|manga}}. It serves as a replacement for the Altars of the [[Altar of the Sunne|Sunne]] and [[Altar of the Moone|Moone]], incorporating elements from both locations into one.

==History==
The Poni Altar first appeared in ''[[PASM24|Play the Melody That Echoes in the Altar]]''. The four [[guardian deities]] of [[Alola]] took {{adv|Sun}} and {{adv|Moon}} there and gave them a [[Sun Flute]] and a [[Moon Flute]], respectively. With the melody of both flutes, Sun and Moon caused the Altar to release a bright light that caused [[Nebby]] and another {{p|Cosmoem}} to [[Evolution|evolve]] into the [[Legendary Pokémon]] {{p|Lunala}} and {{p|Solgaleo}}, respectively.

Shortly afterward, Moon, [[Gladion]], [[Hapu]], and [[Anabel]] fought against a group of [[Ultra Beast]]s that had arrived in Alola. During the clash, a large [[Ultra Wormhole]] opened up with a {{p|Necrozma}}'s hand emerging from it. Necrozma grabbed Solgaleo, taking control of its body. The possessed Solgaleo captured Sun with its tail and dived into the wormhole while Moon and Nebby chased after them.

In ''[[PASM26|Adventure in the Dark Dimension]]'', the aforementioned wormhole was revealed to still be open six months later. In ''[[PASM28|Arrival at the Scientific Megalopolis]]'', [[Lusamine]] was seen at the altar, receiving 100 [[Beast Ball]]s from {{adv|Blake}} disguised as [[Colress]] in preparation for her plan to {{pkmn2|caught|capture}} Necrozma 

In ''[[PASM29|Darkness!! The Mysterious Claws of Necrozma!]]'', [[Phyco]] arrived at the Poni Altar via [[Ultra Warp Ride]] and met Lusamine. She subsequently demonstrated to Phyco how to catch a Pokémon by catching the {{p|Naganadel}} he had used for the Ultra Warp Ride, before asking him to take her to Naganadel's home before they would head to [[Ultra Megalopolis]].
